TITLE: Efficiently Updating Final-Layer Weights for Online Traffic Flow Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Design and compare various linear and nonlinear update strategies for the final-layer weights of a pre-trained traffic flow forecasting model when incorporating newly arrived traffic data. We will update the final-layer weights using online gradient descent, online Newton step, and a recently introduced online Laplace approximation.
CONTROLS: A Wide and Deep model (W2DM) pre-trained on traffic flow data will serve as the base model. We will compare the proposed update strategies with standard online gradient descent on the W2DM. Two common baseline datasets for traffic flow forecasting, PeMSD7 and INMETRO, will be used for evaluation.
COST: 900 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the online Newton step to outperform online gradient descent due to its better estimation of the curvature of the loss function. However, the performance of the online Laplace approximation may suffer from the high variance of the parameter estimates per time step.

PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of different adapter modules on a pre-trained electricity consumption forecasting model when dealing with concept drift in the data. We will train and evaluate a deep neural network with a small adapter module on top of its output and analyze its performance using metrics such as mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and symmetric mean absolute percentage error (sMAPE).
CONTROLS: The base model will be a 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) with 5 layers, pre-trained on historical electricity consumption data. The adapter modules compared will include a single-layer perceptron with 128 units, a two-layer perceptron with 128 units in each layer, and a single-layer LSTM with 128 units. The German Electricity Load Forecasting Dataset will be used for evaluation.
COST: 1350 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the two-layer perceptron to outperform the other adapter modules due to its increased capacity to model complex relationships between the input and output. However, the single-layer LSTM may perform competitively due to its ability to learn sequential dependencies.
